title: Sound Stories & Soundscapes
strapline: Rain on the roof, thunder rolling, birds at dawn — building the sounds of a story with instruments and voices.
intent: Children match sounds to meaning — choosing the right instrument for the rain, the giant's footsteps, the creaking door.
Children listen closely and discriminate between sounds, a key skill for phonics and reading.
Children explore how instruments and voices can be loud, quiet, fast, slow, high and low.
Children collaborate to build a shared soundscape, taking cues and playing together.
Children deepen their love of story by bringing a tale to life through sound.
implementation: Choose a well-loved story and decide together which sound tells each part — shakers for rain, a drum for thunder.
Retell the story and let children play their sound at the right moment, following the narration as a cue.
Listen closely first — what does rain really sound like? light or heavy, fast or slow? — then recreate it.
Explore the qualities of sound: play the same instrument loud then soft, fast then slow, and name the difference.
Build whole soundscapes — a stormy night, a busy morning, a walk in the woods — layering sounds together.
Give children the conductor's role, cueing sounds in and out and controlling loud and quiet.
Record the soundscapes to listen back to, and use voices and body sounds as well as instruments.
key_questions: Which instrument sounds most like the rain — light or heavy?
How could we make the giant's footsteps sound really loud?
What sound comes next in our story?
Can you play it quietly... and now really loud?
What sounds would we hear on a walk in the woods?

impact.text: Children match sounds to meaning, choosing the right instrument for each part of the story.
Children listen closely and discriminate between sounds, building a key skill for phonics.
Children explore loud, quiet, fast, slow, high and low with instruments and voices.
Children collaborate to build a shared soundscape, taking cues and playing together.
Children retell and bring stories to life through sound.
Children take the conductor's role, cueing sounds in and out and controlling volume.

enhancements: A range of instruments — shakers, drums, bells, scrapers, chimes — for different effects.
A well-loved story chosen for its rich sounds.
Picture cards of weather and settings to spark soundscapes.
A recorder to capture and listen back to the soundscapes.
A conductor's baton and 'loud/quiet' signs for cueing.
Body-percussion and voice-sound prompts alongside the instruments.
A listening corner with recorded natural sounds to identify and copy.

playing_exploring: Children explore what each instrument can do and how to make it sound like something real.
They test loud, soft, fast and slow to find the right effect.
active_learning: Children listen and wait for their cue, staying with the story to the end.
They refine a sound until it really captures the rain or the thunder.
creating_thinking: Children choose and combine sounds to represent ideas and feelings.
They invent whole soundscapes and solve how to layer them together.
